metadata.note: Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway, the line that essentially built modern Florida's Atlantic coast. Flagler bought the failing, narrow-gauge Jacksonville, St. Augustine and Halifax River Railway in 1885, converted it to standard gauge, and pushed it south in stages -- reaching St. Augustine (1888), New Smyrna (1892), Cocoa (1893), West Palm Beach (1894), and finally Miami, where the first passenger train arrived April 22 1896 (Miami was a settlement of roughly 300 people at the time). The company was renamed the Florida East Coast Railway on Sept 9 1895, mid-expansion. Flagler kept going: the famous 128-mile 'Overseas Railroad' Key West Extension, built 1905-1912 across open water and islands, opened Jan 1912 and was destroyed beyond repair by the Labor Day Hurricane of 1935 (already in bankruptcy, FEC chose not to rebuild; the right-of-way became part of the Overseas Highway/US 1). The Jacksonville-Miami mainline continued, but a bitter labor strike beginning Jan 22 1963 crippled the railroad; passenger service was suspended, briefly reinstated Jacksonville-North Miami only (Aug 2 1965-Jul 31 1968), then ended for good -- FEC never joined Amtrak in 1971 and ran no passenger trains again until Brightline began using its corridor in 2018 (now drawn separately in brightline.geojson). Geometry is a real-town waypoint approximation, straight-line segments between documented stations -- NOT digitized from period track maps, and the Key West Extension segment in particular is a rough schematic of a genuinely complex multi-island, multi-bridge structure.
sources: https://www.zippia.com/florida-east-coast-railway-careers-23625/history/ (1885 purchase of the Jacksonville, St. Augustine and Halifax River Railway; standard-gauge conversion; renamed Florida East Coast Railway Sept 9 1895; New Smyrna 1892, Cocoa 1893, Palm Beach 1894, Miami service began April 22 1896)
https://www.american-rails.com/key-west.html (Key West Extension built 1905-1912, opened Jan 1912; Labor Day Hurricane 1935 washed out 42 miles of track, line abandoned)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overseas_Railroad (128 miles of open water/islands; Flagler died 1913, one year after completion)

https://locomotive.fandom.com/wiki/Florida_East_Coast_Railway (strike began Jan 22 1963; passenger service reinstated Aug 2 1965 Jacksonville-North Miami only; last regularly scheduled passenger train ran July 31 1968)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact station-by-station mileage; whether the 1888-launched 'Florida Special' (the flagship joint winter train from New York) ran every era modeled here versus other named/local trains; precise island-by-island routing of the Key West Extension.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.brightline_note: 2026-08-25: this layer stops at the end of FEC's own passenger service (July 31 1968). Brightline, which has run over this corridor south of Cocoa since 2018, is a separate operator and lives in data/brightline.geojson -- it is not out of scope for the map (the slider runs to 2026 and Tri-Rail, SunRail and Amtrak are all drawn), it is simply not FEC's own service. Two notes in this file that called Brightline 'outside this map's scope' were corrected to point at that layer.
